title: Interesting News for Starbucks Stock Investors | SBUX Stock Analysis | BROS Stock
creator: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA
summary: He reacts to Starbucks announcing another 250 US/Canada store closures and frames it as evidence of his long-running diseconomies-of-scale thesis: at 40,000+ locations, size is creating inefficiencies rather than advantages. Key arguments: operating margin has collapsed from 18% in 2017 to ~10% now while sales grew (costs rising faster than revenue, driven by dramatic labor cost and wage inflation, especially California's $20+/hour minimum wage); ROIC was above 30% before the pandemic and is now 11-12%, barely at WACC, meaning incremental new locations don't earn their cost of capital. He credits CEO Brian Niccol for identifying the problem and shrinking, but says 250 stores is under 1% of the US/CA count and far more closures are needed. Short term, shrinking may improve profitability; long term, ceding share risks creating a powerful new competitor in Dutch Bros, where he says he is 'a little bullish' on expansion at Starbucks' expense. Valuation: 30x forward PE is rich for a business in this position; his DCF fair value is $66 vs $93 market price. Verdict: SBUX remains a HOLD (reiterated); he'd need a considerably lower price to upgrade to BUY. Other tickers discussed: BROS (bullish tilt, no explicit call).

calls.thesis: Diseconomies of scale: 40k+ stores, op margin 18%->10% since 2017, ROIC near WACC; store closures (250 US/CA) right but more needed; rich at 30x fwd PE, would need considerably lower price to buy.
calls.bull: CEO Brian Niccol's rightsizing lifts near-term profitability.
calls.bear: Ceding NA share invites Dutch Bros as a powerful new competitor.
